question: What is the best first step when building a sewer rehabilitation program for a large collection system?
correctAnswer: Assess the condition and performance of the existing sewers before selecting rehabilitation methods
explanation: Rehabilitation choices depend on verified condition and performance, so assessment comes before method selection, purchasing, or scheduling.
options: Order lining materials for the oldest sewers in the inventory
Assess the condition and performance of the existing sewers before selecting rehabilitation methods
Set construction schedules for every basin in the same year
Buy a new camera truck before reviewing any inspection records
optionA: Order lining materials for the oldest sewers in the inventory
optionB: Assess the condition and performance of the existing sewers before selecting rehabilitation methods
optionC: Set construction schedules for every basin in the same year
optionD: Buy a new camera truck before reviewing any inspection records
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why would a utility complete a basin study before lining sewers in that basin?
correctAnswer: To find where infiltration and other defects are coming from so lining is applied where it will do the most good
explanation: A basin study locates defect and infiltration sources, which lets the program target lining instead of treating every pipe the same way.
options: To avoid cleaning any sewer before the lining crew arrives
To prove that every pipe in the basin needs the same repair
To find where infiltration and other defects are coming from so lining is applied where it will do the most good
To replace the need for post lining inspection
optionA: To avoid cleaning any sewer before the lining crew arrives
optionB: To prove that every pipe in the basin needs the same repair
optionC: To find where infiltration and other defects are coming from so lining is applied where it will do the most good
optionD: To replace the need for post lining inspection
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Sewer Rehabilitation Program Planning. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why are sewers cleaned and inspected by camera before a liner is installed?
correctAnswer: Cleaning and inspection reveal roots, deposits, and defects that could prevent a proper liner installation
explanation: Roots, deposits, and hidden defects can block or distort a liner, so the host pipe is cleaned and inspected first.
options: Cleaning and inspection reveal roots, deposits, and defects that could prevent a proper liner installation
Cleaning makes the host pipe diameter larger for the next size of liner
Inspection removes the need to check lateral connections after lining
A clean pipe guarantees the liner will never need maintenance
optionA: Cleaning and inspection reveal roots, deposits, and defects that could prevent a proper liner installation
optionB: Cleaning makes the host pipe diameter larger for the next size of liner
optionC: Inspection removes the need to check lateral connections after lining
optionD: A clean pipe guarantees the liner will never need maintenance
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: A sewer is cracked and leaking but keeps its shape and alignment, and digging up the street would be highly disruptive. Which rehabilitation approach fits best?
correctAnswer: Trenchless lining of the existing pipe
explanation: A pipe that holds its shape and alignment can usually accept a trenchless liner, avoiding disruptive excavation.
options: Full open cut replacement of the entire street
Leaving the pipe in service with no repair planned
Jetting the pipe repeatedly until the cracks close
Trenchless lining of the existing pipe
optionA: Full open cut replacement of the entire street
optionB: Leaving the pipe in service with no repair planned
optionC: Jetting the pipe repeatedly until the cracks close
optionD: Trenchless lining of the existing pipe

question: In a rehabilitation program, what is joint grouting mainly used to do?
correctAnswer: Seal leaking joints and stop infiltration at those joints
explanation: Grouting seals leaking joints from inside the pipe, which cuts infiltration at the joint without replacing the pipe.
options: Seal leaking joints and stop infiltration at those joints
Increase the diameter of a sewer that is too small
Replace a collapsed pipe with a new pipe
Remove grease deposits from a sewer wall
optionA: Seal leaking joints and stop infiltration at those joints
optionB: Increase the diameter of a sewer that is too small
optionC: Replace a collapsed pipe with a new pipe
optionD: Remove grease deposits from a sewer wall

Lowest bid price and shortest detour route
Age of the newest pipe and size of the annual budget for vehicles
Likelihood of failure and consequence of failure

explanation: Failure of a large trunk under a major road near a watercourse affects many customers, traffic, and the environment at once.

A large trunk sewer under a major arterial road near a watercourse
A small local sewer in an open field with easy access
A new sewer with a full warranty and no customers upstream
optionA: A short residential lateral on a quiet cul de sac
optionB: A large trunk sewer under a major arterial road near a watercourse
optionC: A small local sewer in an open field with easy access
